stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \frac{4x^{3}}{1 - 7x} \). Find the first 4 nonzero terms and the general term of the Maclaurin series for f.

worked_solution.text: Start from the Maclaurin series for \( \frac{1}{1 - x} \) and replace x by \( 7x \), raising the whole of \( 7x \) to each power.
Multiply every term by \( 4 x^{3} \); the first 4 nonzero terms are \( 4 x^{3} + 28 x^{4} + 196 x^{5} + 1372 x^{6} \).
The general term is \( 4 \cdot 7^{n} x^{n+3} \); putting n = 0, 1, 2 reproduces the terms above.

options.label: \( 4 x^{3} + 28 x^{4} + 196 x^{5} + 1372 x^{6} + \cdots + 4 \cdot 7^{n+1} x^{n+4} + \cdots \)
options.derivation: the general term written with n + 1 where n belongs, so at n = 0 it gives the second term rather than the first

options.label: \( 4 x^{3} - 28 x^{4} + 196 x^{5} - 1372 x^{6} + \cdots + 4 \cdot (-1)^{n} 7^{n} x^{n+3} + \cdots \)
options.derivation: the series for 1/(1 - x) recalled with alternating signs, as for 1/(1 + x)

options.label: \( 4 x^{3} + 28 x^{4} + 28 x^{5} + 28 x^{6} + \cdots + 4 \cdot 7 x^{n+3} + \cdots \)
options.derivation: x replaced by 7x but 7 not raised to the power of each term
